# TheoryA.ai

> TheoryA.ai develops and applies Theory A, a management philosophy of organizational design for the age of AI. Theory A holds that organizations are designed around assumptions, that those assumptions drive structure and structure drives behavior, and that abundant intelligence has made many inherited assumptions obsolete. TheoryA.ai works inside corporate functions: Human Resources, Information Technology, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and the shared services that deliver them. Founded by Emily Liddle and Jim Scully.

Theory A is organized around five principles, each an enduring design question: Abundance (what economic reality are you designing for?), Outcome (what is the organization fundamentally organizing around?), Orchestration (how are different forms of agency designed to work together?), Form (what structures create or constrain agency?), and Compounding (does the system increase or dissipate organizational capability over time?). Theory A distinguishes three forms of agency: human, organizational, and artificial.

TheoryA.ai's work is published in Collections, each authored and governed by an Expert Author, and made conversational through Digital Intelligence, an extension of a specific Expert Author's judgment trained on their Collection. Signals are short public essays. Provocations are longer public arguments, one per Collection.

## Core

- [Home](https://theorya.ai/): What Theory A is, the five principles, and how TheoryA.ai works with organizations

- [Organizing Agency: The Theory A Manifesto](https://theorya.ai/manifesto): The full statement of Theory A
